name: Minimalist Product Motion Design
visualIdentity: A descriptive, normalized product presentation direction: one accurately rendered product, a few meaningful details, generous space, concise copy, precise proportions, restrained materials and light, smooth close-ups, selective reveals, and deliberate settling. Avoid copying specific campaign shots.
suitableUses: Explicitly suited to product explainers, hero reveals, premium launches, product introductions, and spec callouts. For interactive HTML, a centered product hero or optional gallery can use scroll-linked framing; suitability beyond these uses is inferred from its restrained, product-focused presentation.
limitations: Product accuracy is essential; preserve source imagery, interfaces, materials, logos, and brand colors. Restraint is central, so hybrids should be limited to framing or a few spec lines. Do not add props, clutter, or motion that obscures the product. Any 3D dolly needs real depth or a disclosed 2.5D approximation; flat-image scaling is a zoom. Exact duration, aspect ratio, and production assets are unspecified.
palette: There is no intrinsic canonical palette. The optional fallback for new presentation elements is background #F6F2EA and foreground #2A3030, with one dominant background and clear foreground hierarchy. These are suggestions only: task, brand, approved reference, and existing semantic colors take precedence. Preserve product and asset colors exactly; do not recolor, expand hues, or add gradients. The supplied opaque text pair has a 12.026 contrast ratio, but actual compositing must be checked.
motionAndInteraction: Use purposeful details and camera moves, smooth close-ups, selective reveals, and deliberate settling; preserve sharp cuts, impacts, constant-speed sections, and reading holds where intended. For video, all states must be deterministic and seekable. HyperFrames is the primary composition and export pipeline; Remotion is a documented, conditional fallback only. GSAP owns the registered paused master timeline; optional motion libraries require verified time synchronization and separate property ownership. Interactive HTML may add scroll-linked hero framing, accessible card navigation or galleries, and reduced-motion states. Exploded reveals require meaningful separable components; a dolly requires real depth. Avoid unsupported catalog motions.
audio: No fixed soundtrack or mandatory audio layer is specified. Choose music, voice, effects, ambience, or silence for the subject and audience; honor supplied audio choices. Keep speech intelligible and synchronize, mix, and inspect audio with picture in the selected render pipeline.
assetRequirements: Use accurate product imagery or genuine 3D models when needed; Blender can create models, materials, lighting, animation, and offline renders. SVG suits crisp interface elements, shapes, masks, and details. Preserve source assets and exact colors. Crop preparation is optional and must retain product proportions, logos, key features, and motion margins. Load fonts and assets before animation; do not assume photographic assets exist.
combinations: Usually best alone. Optional style-104 symmetry can support centered hero shots; retain the two palette tokens and avoid theatrical props. Optional style-093 can add short specs or a tagline, one moving line at a time, clear of the product silhouette, with reading holds and no expressive spring or scale motion. Use other motion patterns only when their actual geometry and narrative fit the scene.
productionApproach: Choose the visual renderer and motion engine for the product and required fidelity, then use the composition pipeline only for assembly, timing, media/audio sync, validation, and export. SVG and Blender are recommended style tools; Leaflet is conditional on genuine geographic context. Use only needed libraries, with one owner per animated property. Prepare and load assets, drive video from shared composition time, and verify representative frames, direct and backward seeks, full playback, and audio sync. For HTML interactions, provide usable keyboard/touch controls and reduced-motion behavior where relevant. The supplied metadata does not establish actual locally installed tools or source-video production methods.
